final_prompt_en: Make a school-life photograph of a student character, capturing a moment of school life at the end of a baking practical. A fictional adult woman stands beside her workbench in a home-economics classroom, wearing a white school blouse with sleeves folded to the elbows, a narrow navy neck ribbon, and a navy pleated uniform skirt. A pale blue cotton bib apron lies over the uniform, its waist ties wrapped forward and knotted at the front; flour on the apron and a tray of golden bread cooling beside her connect her clothing to the work she has just finished. Use the supplied photograph as the visual guide for her facial appearance and hair: a dark chin-length bob, separated wispy fringe, brown eyes, and a softly rounded facial contour. Render her as this fictional character in the new scene. Her left hand steadies the front waist knot while her right hand draws one loose tie sideways through the bow; the slackening loop and both fingers meeting the apron ties are clearly visible together. Her elbows remain comfortably beside her waist, shoulders lowered, weight settled through both legs. She glances from the knot toward the cooling bread with a small, relieved smile, as if checking the result before finally taking a break. The apron still hangs from its neck strap and covers the front of her skirt as the waist fastening loosens. Behind her, school worktables, stools and a chalkboard with a simple baking diagram establish the class setting. A vertical knees-up photograph from a gently frontal three-quarter position keeps her face, both forearms, waist fastening and bread tray in the same clear view. Soft afternoon window light gives her face and rumpled cotton a tactile warmth; the hands and loosened knot carry the transition from concentration to ease, with the classroom receding quietly behind her.

pixel_gate_results.evidence: The same foreground wearer stands among multiple instructional cooking stations with pots and stools; the board shows bread-stage drawings. This is a practical-class setting rather than costume alone.

The face remains in clear upper-frame view, with a dark chin-length bob, separated fringe, brown eyes and softly rounded contour broadly consistent with the source portrait. This is visual resemblance only; real identity, age and biography remain unknown.

White blouse, navy ribbon and pleated navy skirt remain distinct beneath a pale blue flour-marked bib apron, and neck/waist support is coherent. However the front bow still has a compact central knot and taut folded loops; the required visibly loosening state is not established. Visible garment layers alone cannot pass the full gate.

At native scale both hands are visible gripping folded fabric on opposite sides of the central bow. The subject right hand (image left) holds a folded loop and the subject left hand (image right) holds the other loop away from the knot; neither clearly steadies the central knot while the other pulls a free tail through it. Two free ends still hang below the intact knot. The intended support-plus-free-tail-pull/slackening relation is absent; ordinary bow handling is insufficient.

Flour is visible over the worn apron front, and golden completed bread sits on a cooling rack/tray on the adjacent workbench in the same frame as the wearer. These cues connect clothing and finished practical work without needing the prompt story.

Face, both connected forearms and hands, front waist fastening and bread are all retained in a clear foreground hierarchy. Arms reach the waist coherently and the standing trunk/upper legs are balanced. The physical ownership and reach are readable; the specific unfastening-state defect is recorded separately above.

observed_pixel_limitation: Both hands grip opposite folded bow loops rather than one steadying the central knot while the other pulls a loose free tail. The central bow remains compact; the required loosening result is not established.
